status: prospective candidate; no adaptation outcome inspected
question: If source initialization helps on SHIFT-SUV, is the benefit driven by nearby vehicle geometry, reusable external-flow response experience, or source diversity?
activation_gate: Do not launch this comparison unless the validation-only DrivAerML adaptation pilot shows a reusable-initialization effect worth explaining.

prospective_matched_sources.name: mixed
prospective_matched_sources.composition: a fixed 435-case mixture split as evenly as possible between DrivAerML and HighLiftAeroML

fairness_requirements: Use the same architecture, source-example count, source optimization budget, target subsets, and target adaptation rule across source conditions.
Train only the two target-compatible physical fields under common nondimensional conventions.
Freeze source subsets and all target-selection rules before inspecting adaptation outcomes.

rival_predictions.geometry_scaffold: The vehicle source transfers better than the aircraft source, and the matched mixture does not improve on the vehicle source.
rival_predictions.response_reuse: The geometry-distant aircraft source still improves over scratch on both target body styles.
rival_predictions.diversity: The matched mixture improves on both single-domain sources despite containing fewer vehicle cases.
rival_predictions.specialist_families: The aircraft source is neutral or harmful and no source ordering is stable across target body styles.

limits: Vehicle versus aircraft also changes flow regime, so one comparison cannot fully separate geometry from every notion of response compatibility.
A source effect shared by both architectures would support reusable data experience, not a boundary-specific architectural claim.
Source-checkpoint quality and target-training seed uncertainty require explicit controls before any test split is opened.
